In many Shona families, the custom of a woman going to her parents' home for the birth of her first child.

front: Who digs the grave at many indigenous funerals?
Name four stages of indigenous death rites.
back: Any four of: announcing the death, preparing the body, the wake, burial, cleansing, mourning, kurova guva/umbuyiso.

front: Why did mother and baby stay indoors after birth?
back: To rest and to be protected from infection and harm while relatives did the work.

front: What do the names Rudo, Tendai and Themba mean?
back: Rudo: love. Tendai: be thankful. Themba: hope.

front: Give three reasons why death rites matter.
back: Unity and support for the bereaved; respect for the dead and, for many, the link with the ancestors; teaching the young how to behave.

front: Name three threats to birth and death rites.
back: Urbanisation and migration; rising costs; religious change; hospitals, mortuaries and funeral companies taking over family tasks.
